deviations: The task's Verify+close step 3 said to write this closure JSON and 'include it in the same commit' as the one T1 commit, and also asked for 'commit_sha' inside that same JSON. These two requirements are in tension: a commit's SHA is a hash of its own tree, so a file committed as part of that commit cannot exactly contain that commit's final SHA (writing the SHA changes the tree, which changes the SHA). I resolved this pragmatically: committed the 3 content changes first, captured that HEAD SHA, wrote this JSON with `commit_sha` set to the SHA of the (single, un-amended) commit that already held the content changes, then `git commit --amend --no-edit` to fold this JSON file into that same commit (still exactly one commit on doc-hygiene-1, message unchanged). The amend changed the actual HEAD SHA one more time -- so `commit_sha` above is the pre-JSON intermediate SHA (`1a4961abb467da4c04f026dc8c2d75ae8864d37b`), which is one amend behind the true final HEAD. Nothing was force-pushed or amended after sharing; the amend only ever touched the single commit this agent itself just created on this branch. The true final HEAD SHA is reported in my closing message to the orchestrator (`git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD` is the source of truth, not this field).
